recall.define: For Linux kernel programming and lifetime boundaries, define module init unwind, publication boundary (module), user-copy residual, staged kernel publication, reference handoff (kernel), reference resurrection, raw spin context, CPU-local exclusion, work quiescence, admission closure, retirement (RCU model), reader grace obligation, kernel wire ABI, compatibility admission, module text lifetime, detached device owner, giving each invariant.
recall.distinguish: For Linux kernel programming and lifetime boundaries, distinguish these near concepts: module init unwind versus module exit; publication boundary (module) versus allocation; user-copy residual versus completed count; staged kernel publication versus partial copy; reference handoff (kernel) versus pointer copy; reference resurrection versus protected lookup; raw spin context versus ordinary RT spin lock; CPU-local exclusion versus cross-CPU serialization; work quiescence versus cancellation request; admission closure versus drain; retirement (RCU model) versus reclamation; reader grace obligation versus timer delay; kernel wire ABI versus native struct layout; compatibility admission versus authorization; module text lifetime versus object lifetime; detached device owner versus registered device.
recall.apply: Reuse kernel.module_owner in the completion-owner domain; compare object lifetime, module text lifetime and device lifetime, which are three distinct resources.
